questions.q: In Commerce, a market is best defined as
options: only a physical building where traders store their goods
any arrangement or medium that brings buyers and sellers into contact to exchange goods and services
a government-owned institution that prints the nation's currency
the specific geographical area where heavy manufacturing takes place
questions.explain: In business studies, a **market** is not just a physical place. It is any medium (such as a physical shop, a website, or a telephone network) that enables buyers and sellers to interact and exchange goods and services.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental feature of a market?
options: The presence of buyers and sellers
A medium of exchange or price
The presence of a commercial bank manager
A commodity or service to be exchanged
questions.explain: The essential features of a market include **buyers**, **sellers**, **goods/services**, and a **price** (medium of exchange). The presence of a commercial bank manager is not a fundamental requirement for a market to exist.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The financial market where short-term funds, loans, and securities are bought and sold is known as the
questions.explain: The **money market** is the financial market designed for the lending and borrowing of short-term funds (usually for a period of up to one year).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Businesses and governments use which type of market to raise long-term funds for major investments and expansion?
questions.explain: The **capital market** specializes in medium and long-term funds. Organizations issue shares and long-term bonds in this market to raise capital for long-term investments.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A market specialized in the buying and selling of primary agricultural goods and solid minerals like cocoa, cotton, and gold is the
questions.explain: The **commodity market** deals specifically with the bulk trading of raw primary products (commodities) such as crude oil, gold, cocoa, and wheat.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following acts as a primary institution in the money market?
questions.explain: **Commercial banks** are the primary institutions operating in the money market. They provide short-term loans, overdrafts, and discount bills of exchange for traders.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The principal institution in the capital market where existing company shares and government bonds are openly traded is the
questions.explain: The **Stock Exchange** is the main institution of the capital market. It provides a highly organized floor where stockbrokers buy and sell existing securities like shares and bonds.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An example of a financial instrument traded in the money market is the
questions.explain: A **Treasury Bill** is a short-term debt instrument issued by the government, making it a money market instrument. Shares, bonds, and debentures are long-term instruments traded in the capital market.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following financial instruments is used by public limited companies to raise long-term capital in the capital market?
questions.explain: **Equities (Shares)** represent ownership units in a company and are the primary instruments sold in the capital market to raise long-term, permanent business capital.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A registered professional agent authorized to buy and sell securities on the Stock Exchange on behalf of investors is called a
questions.explain: A **stockbroker** acts as an intermediary or agent on the floor of the Stock Exchange, buying and selling shares for their clients in exchange for a commission.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognized professional career path in the Capital Market?
questions.explain: A **Portfolio Manager** (or investment analyst) is a career in the capital market involving managing a collection of investments (like shares and bonds) on behalf of clients.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The foundational commercial process of acquiring goods by giving up an equivalent value in money is known as
questions.explain: In the concept of trading, **buying** is the act of acquiring ownership of goods and services in exchange for money, while selling is giving them up for money.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business transaction in which goods are exchanged and immediate payment is made simultaneously is called a
questions.explain: A **cash transaction** occurs when a buyer pays for goods immediately at the time of purchase using physical cash, cheques, or instant electronic transfers.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When a customer collects bags of rice from a wholesaler but agrees to pay the money at the end of the month, the process is referred to as buying by
questions.explain: Buying by **credit** means goods are delivered and accepted immediately, but the payment of the agreed amount is postponed to a future date.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The total monetary value of all net sales made by a business during a specific financial period is known as
questions.explain: **Turnover** refers to the total net sales revenue generated by a business over a specific period (usually a year), before deducting any costs or expenses.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The total expenditure incurred by a business strictly on purchasing or manufacturing the actual goods that were sold is referred to as the
questions.explain: The **cost of sale** (or Cost of Goods Sold) represents the direct costs involved in bringing the goods to a saleable condition (e.g., buying price plus carriage inwards).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: In a commercial transaction, what is realized when the selling price of an article is greater than its cost price?
questions.explain: **Profit** is the positive financial difference obtained when the Selling Price (SP) is higher than the Cost Price (CP). Thus, $\text{Profit} = \text{SP} - \text{CP}$.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A trader bought a carton of biscuits for $\text{N}3,500$ and later sold it to a final consumer for $\text{N}5,000$. Calculate the profit.
questions.explain:
The formula for profit is: $$\text{Profit} = \text{Selling Price} - \text{Cost Price}$$
$\text{Profit} = \text{N}5,000 - \text{N}3,500 = \text{N}1,500$.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The ratio of the profit made on a good expressed as a percentage or fraction of the **cost price** is known as
questions.explain: **Mark up** is the profit calculated as a percentage of the cost price. It shows how much extra was 'marked up' on top of the original cost to arrive at the selling price.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A retail business has an Opening Stock of $\text{N}20,000$, total Purchases for the year amounting to $\text{N}50,000$, and a Closing Stock of $\text{N}10,000$. What is the Cost of Sales?
questions.explain:
The formula for Cost of Sales is: $$\text{Opening Stock} + \text{Purchases} - \text{Closing Stock}$$
Cost of Sales = $\text{N}20,000 + \text{N}50,000 - \text{N}10,000 = \text{N}60,000$.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Calculate the Mark up percentage if a trader buys a radio for $\text{N}4,000$ and sells it for $\text{N}5,000$.
questions.explain:
First, calculate Profit: $\text{N}5,000 - \text{N}4,000 = \text{N}1,000$.
Next, apply the Mark up formula: $$\text{Mark up} = \frac{\text{Profit}}{\text{Cost Price}} \times 100$$
$$\frac{1,000}{4,000} \times 100 = 25\%$$.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: If a boutique sells $150$ shirts during the year at a uniform price of $\text{N}3,000$ each, what is the annual turnover of the boutique?
questions.explain:
**Turnover** represents total sales.
$$\text{Turnover} = \text{Quantity Sold} \times \text{Selling Price}$$
Turnover = $150 \times \text{N}3,000 = \text{N}450,000$.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Commerce & Activities That Aid Commerce
questions.subject: Business Studies
